obligations.seam: every mutating verb on CLI, MCP tool and /api/ endpoint
obligations.behavior: without --apply / apply=true (JSON boolean) the transport sends zero write APDUs and the result carries the planned per-block diff
obligations.source_text: Tag-mutating verbs (write, restore, ndef write, format/lock) are dry-run by default and only touch the tag with --apply; dry-run reports exactly which pages/blocks would change (diff against current contents)

obligations.behavior: sector trailers (block 3 of each sector) and block 0 are never written unless include_trailers is explicitly set; the dry-run diff lists them as skipped
obligations.source_text: Restore never writes sector trailers (block 3 of each sector) or manufacturer block 0 unless --include-trailers is passed explicitly; a wrong access-bits write permanently bricks a MIFARE Classic sector

obligations.behavior: trailers are written only from the fixed NFC-Forum template; access bits are parity-checked before any write APDU and an invalid template aborts with exit 2 before touching the tag
obligations.source_text: NDEF on MIFARE Classic (the X3 and the transparent sticker) requires formatting per the NFC Forum / NXP MIFARE Classic NDEF mapping: MAD in sector 0 with key A A0A1A2A3A4A5 and NDEF sectors with key A D3F7D3F7D3F7 and NDEF access bits — i.e. writing sector trailers, which c23 forbids without --include-trailers (from memory of NXP AN1304/AN1305, not re-read this session)

obligations.behavior: a pre-write snapshot of the target tag is written (0600) and its path reported before the first write APDU; if the snapshot fails, no write is sent
obligations.source_text: Before any --apply write (write, restore, ndef write/erase/format) the current readable contents of the target tag are snapshotted to a timestamped dump file (0600, under the user data dir) and its path is printed; 'tag restore SNAPSHOT --apply' is the documented rollback

obligations.behavior: every write is followed by a read-back compare; a mismatch or dropout stops the operation, exits 2, and leaves a resumable journal listing written/verified/pending blocks
obligations.source_text: Writes are journaled: each block/page write is followed by a read-back compare and appended to a per-operation journal; an interrupted restore (card lifted, USB error) reports written/verified/pending blocks and 'tag restore --resume JOURNAL' completes it

obligations.seam: USB interface claim (CLI, MCP, ui serve)
obligations.behavior: the interface is claimed per operation and released after; a busy reader exits 2 naming the lock holder; no long-lived process holds the claim while idle
obligations.source_text: Reader access is exclusive (probe: second process claiming interface 0 gets USBError 16 Resource busy). Every operation claims and releases the interface, an advisory lock file under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR records the holder (pid + command), and a busy reader raises CliError exit 2 naming the holder (e.g. 'nfc-cli ui serve', or pcscd if installed later) instead of a raw USBError; ui serve and mcp never hold the interface between operations

obligations.behavior: USBError, EACCES, no card, card removed, auth failure and SW != 9000 surface as CliError exit 2 with a hint: line; no library exception or traceback reaches _dispatch
obligations.source_text: Hardware failures (no reader, permission denied, no card, card removed, auth failure, APDU status != 9000) are caught in handlers and raised as CliError with EXIT_ENV_ERROR (2) and a concrete hint; library exceptions never reach _dispatch, which would mislabel them EXIT_USER_ERROR with 'file a bug'

obligations.seam: dump/journal files and every output surface
obligations.behavior: files are created 0600 outside the repo by default; key bytes are masked in text, --trace, MCP and API output unless include_keys is set
obligations.source_text: Dumps and journals contain sector keys/trailers: files are written 0600, keys are masked in text output and traces, and MCP/API responses redact key bytes unless the caller passes include_keys; dumps never land inside the repo tree by default (scan-secrets would not catch binary/hex keys)

obligations.behavior: any polling-type change is restored in an independent step and verified by read-back (07 05 factory); HID keyboard / operating-mode escapes are never sent
obligations.source_text: Reader configuration is read-mostly: the CLI may read reader settings and set the PICC polling type only with snapshot-then-restore in an independent step that verifies by read-back; it never sets the HID keyboard / operating mode (E0 00 00 9x), because 'Only HID Keyboard' mode removes the CCID interface the CLI depends on

obligations.behavior: the reader is returned to Card Read/Write mode on normal exit, Ctrl-C, or error, verified by a follow-up read/write-mode probe
obligations.source_text: Card emulation (ISO 18092 mode of the ACR1552, manual §6.1.15): 'nfc-cli emulate type2|felica' puts the reader into emulation (E0 00 00 40 03 02|03 00 00) with programmable UID and loads a 2000-byte Type 2 memory image (e.g. an NDEF record or a dump's NDEF) so a phone tapping the reader sees a tag; always returns the reader to Card Read/Write mode on exit, Ctrl-C, or error, verified by read-back

obligations.behavior: a request without the install secret or with a non-allow-listed Origin/Host gets 401/403 and causes no USB traffic
obligations.source_text: Mutating /api/ endpoints are guarded: install secret in a 0600 file sent as Authorization header plus Host/Origin allow-list — loopback is not authentication (embodiment CLAUDE.md:362), and a browser tab on another origin must not be able to write a tag via DNS rebinding/CSRF

obligations.behavior: a non-loopback --host without --bind-public exits 1 with a hint and never opens a socket
obligations.source_text: Python side serves the UI with stdlib http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer (zero new runtime deps): static bundle at /, JSON API under /api/ (reader status, tag info/read/write/dump/restore, ndef read/write), loopback-only by default with resolve_bind refusing routable addresses unless --bind-public, own default port distinct from embodiment's 8823 and culture-rules' 8765/8791/8796

obligations.behavior: the MCP tool-name set equals the CLI verb-path set (parity test); boolean args must be JSON booleans; mutating tools dry-run unless apply is exactly true
obligations.source_text: MCP server: 'nfc-cli mcp' serves every CLI verb as an MCP tool over stdio (optional 'mcp' extra, lazily imported, mcp>=1.2,<2), tools named <noun>_<verb>, mutating tools dry-run unless apply is exactly JSON true, and a parity test keeps CLI and MCP surfaces identical — so agents can drive the reader via CLI or MCP

obligations.behavior: importing nfc_cli and running identity verbs needs no third-party package; usb/web/mcp extras are imported lazily and a missing extra exits 2 with the pip install hint
obligations.source_text: Base install stays zero-third-party-dependency: pyusb (usb) and any web server stack sit behind optional extras (e.g. nfc-cli[usb], nfc-cli[web]) imported lazily; a missing extra raises CliError EXIT_ENV_ERROR with an install hint — mirroring culture-rules serve.py

obligations.seam: tag verbs on a weakly coupled tag
obligations.behavior: --wait polls for presence up to the timeout; a dropout mid-dump resumes per sector and the dump completes or exits 2 with what was read
obligations.source_text: RF coupling with the X3 is marginal (detected only after ~18 s of repositioning, dropped out between runs): tag verbs need --wait/--timeout to poll for presence, and dump/restore must resume per sector after dropouts and verify every write by reading back
